claims.text: The general cleaning agent specified for grease or oil on metal parts is a mild detergent or a solvent such as mineral spirits or a petroleum-based cleaner.
Mild detergents and solvents such as mineral spirits or petroleum-based cleaners are commonly used because of effectiveness in removing oils and greases without damaging metal surfaces.
The general cleaning choice must not be applied to the CDR (Cylinder Drain Valve).
The CDR valve contains sensitive internal components, including seals and precision parts.
Solvents or detergents may damage the CDR valve's sensitive internal components by degrading rubber or plastic materials or causing corrosion.

TM 9-2320-280-20-1, Volume 1 (1996, including Change 2 dated 2004), specifies cleaning the CDR valve with a clean, dry cloth and a non-abrasive, non-oil-based cleaning agent specifically approved for use on rubber and plastic components.
The CDR valve should be wiped gently with a clean, lint-free cloth to remove surface dirt or debris.
No solvent or oil-based cleaning agents should be used on the CDR valve.
